artifacts.title: Psiaki v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained Psiaki’s complaint and held that the CPC Session erred by ordaining and installing officers elected at a February 5, 2023 congregational meeting where the congregation’s bylaw excluded communing members under 18 from voting. Reading BCO 6-4, 25-1, and 25-7 together, the SJC ruled that all communing members are entitled to vote and that local bylaws cannot impose an age restriction; the “good and regular standing” language addresses censure, not age. The decision did not annul the completed ordination/installation, but required future elections and installations to comply with the Constitution.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained an appeal by seven members of a 38-member mission church who were convicted by their temporary Session of opposing the organizing minister's expected election as pastor. Reversing the Presbytery's affirmance and the guilty verdicts underlying indefinite suspensions, the SJC held the indictments fatally lacked BCO 32-5 specificity; Presbytery used the wrong standard of review; the Session had no authority to control pastoral selection; and no Fifth or Ninth Commandment offense was proved. Challenges to witness-judges, venue, and refusal to refer were rejected.

artifacts.title: Reese and Bech v. Philadelphia Presbytery

matches.evidence: …to a survey by Presbytery regarding Diaconal practices: - a) As allowed in BCO 5-10 and 9-2 we do not plan to establish a formal diaconate at the time of particularization.…
- **a)** As allowed in BCO 5-10 and 9-2 we do not plan to establish a formal diaconate at the time of particularization.

artifacts.synopsis: Philadelphia Presbytery declared Reese and Bech's complaint out of order because some supporting reasons and requested amends allegedly violated the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding Presbytery misapplied Robert's Rules: objectionable parts do not justify rejecting an entire complaint, and a court need not adopt requested amends. It also said pertinent questions about whether a call is for the good of the Church may be asked, but agreed the amends—including removing TE Hsu—were inappropriate and could not rescind his installation.

artifacts.title: Appointing unordained men and women to diaconal ministry roles

matches.evidence: CCB found an overture appointing unordained persons to diaconal ministry in conflict with the Constitution, including because it implied an unordained office contrary to BCO 17-1.
